..
Issued at 239 AM CDT Mon Oct 12 2026

A closed upper low was noted over the Pacific Northwest and Northern 
Rockies per the 07Z water vapor imagery while upper ridging remained 
over the lower and middle MS river valley. Surface obs indicated an 
area of low pressure over northeast CO that has allowed good 
southerly low level flow from the TX gulf coast through the central 
plains. Richer moisture in the form of higher surface dewpoints had 
just begun to return through south TX. Meanwhile a weak stationary 
surface boundary extended from CO east through central and northeast 
NEB. 

For today and tonight the forecast area is expected to remain mainly 
between the upper low to the west and upper ridging to the 
southeast. Models show an upper jet rotating through the base of the 
upper low with the right exit region of this jet influencing general 
subsidence across northeast KS this afternoon. Meanwhile the better 
low level moisture advection is progged to hold off until the 
overnight time frame. So models don't show much instability or 
forcing for precip. The one exception is the potential for some 
elevated showers developing within a warm air advection pattern near 
the NEB state line this evening. RAP and NAM isentropic surfaces 
show the better saturation within the lift staying just north of the 
forecast area. Nevertheless the 00Z HRRR develops some isolated 
shower activity across the northwestern counties. So can't 
completely rule out a brief shower and have some slight chance POPs 
near the state line. After midnight, the saturation lifts further 
north and east of the forecast area and should take any precip with 
it. 

Models seem to be converging on a common solution with the pattern 
for Tuesday through Thursday with lower spread from the ensembles. 
Initially the forecast area will be under southwest flow aloft with 
the frontal boundary over NEB sagging south into parts of north 
central and northeast KS by Tuesday afternoon. This boundary looks 
to act as a focus for convection development but with most guidance 
indicating low level flow veered to the southwest ahead of the 
boundary, it may take some time for storms to initiate. It may be 
that storms develop southwest of the area and translate northeast 
along the front. In any case bulk shear around 50KT with a corridor 
of 2000 to 3000 J/kg of surface based CAPE will be supportive of 
severe storms and perhaps supercell thunderstorms. Large hail and 
damaging winds look to be the main concern with any tornado risk 
conditional on whether low level winds can back enough to increase 
SRH. Storms also look to be efficient rain producers as PWs increase 
to around 2 inches. This would be a record value for precipital 
water and 2 to 3 standard deviations above the climatological mean. 
So we'll have to keep an eye out for flooding, especially if the 
frontal boundary is slow to move. 

By Wednesday most guidance has the surface front pushing into east 
central KS with a lead shortwave lifting over the area. This wave 
could enhance the low level moisture advection over the frontal 
boundary with continued showers and storms during the day. Limited 
insolation and the front sliding south may prevent much 
destabilization and the risk for severe storms across east central 
KS. The better synoptic scale dynamics with the system are progged 
to impact the area Wednesday night and into Thursday morning as a 
weak surface wave lifts northeast along the boundary. The NBM keeps 
some categorical POPs across east central KS for this and see no 
reason to change it. Did however adjust highs cooler for Wednesday 
anticipating cloud cover and precip to inhibit a strong warm up. 
Still highs ranging from the middle 60s to the middle 70s may be a 
little warm if precip persists for much of the day. By the time the 
system exits to the east Thursday night, parts of east central KS 
could receive between 1 and 3 inches of rain and later shifts may 
want to consider a flood watch. 

As the surface waves lifts past the forecast area Thursday evening, 
high pressure with increasing dry air advection is progged to build 
into the area. This should bring much cooler temperatures to the 
region for Friday and Saturday. A more zonal pattern is progged to 
develop late in the forecast period allowing southerly low level 
winds to redevelop by Sunday. This should allow temps to trend a 
little warmer into the 70s.
